title: Guiding LLM Decision-Making with Fairness Reward Models
findings: The proposed Fairness Reward Model (FRM) significantly reduced fairness gaps related to religion. In the Civil Comments moderation task, the FRM caused the equalized odds gap between comments mentioning Christianity and Islam to fall by more than ten percentage points from a baseline exceeding sixty percentage points, without harming, and in some cases even improving, accuracy.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured disparities in toxicity judgments for social media comments that mentioned different religious groups (Christian vs. Muslim). The goal was to reduce the fairness gap (measured by equalized odds and equalized opportunity) in these moderation decisions.
